reason: The text explicitly demonstrates both elements of the statement. In Exodus 32:9-10, after the golden calf incident, Yahweh tells Moses: 'I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people: Now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them: and I will make of thee a great nation.' This passage directly shows God (1) expressing willingness to abandon loyalty to the people by consuming them, and (2) explicitly considering replacing them with a new nation to be made from Moses's descendants. The text clearly portrays God as considering the people replaceable and demonstrating no commitment to preserving them despite their covenant history.
